alt: The “library is a promise” paragraph with each device labelled: “promise” repeated, “It” referring to the library, three parallel “it promises that...” clauses, “this promise” referring back, and a final shift to “something more than a building”. A table summarises repetition, synonyms, pronoun reference and parallel structure.
caption: Repetition, synonyms, pronouns and parallelism tell readers which ideas belong together.

alt: Lincoln’s near-synonyms dedicate, consecrate and hallow rise like steps in sacredness. Below, “the council decided”, “ruled” and “dictated” describe one event with different suggestions about how it was done.
caption: A synonym varies the word but also shifts the meaning: use that on purpose.

alt: Four pronoun problems with repairs: an ambiguous “he” (the mayor or the engineer), a missing antecedent for “they”, a vague “This”, and a distant antecedent. A habit box recommends following “this”, “that” and “it” with a noun.
caption: If the reader cannot tell what a pronoun stands for, name the noun.

alt: Two faulty lists (“hiking, to swim and bicycles”; “save money, improving safety and to reduce delays”) beside their parallel repairs. Below, deliberate parallelism showing equality (Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness), rhythm (of the people, by the people, for the people), contrast (To err is human, to forgive, divine) and inevitability (Paine).
caption: Parallelism means the same grammatical form, not the same words.

alt: Three repairs to the committee passage. Pronouns: vague “they”, “It”, “which” and “They” become “who”, “The change” and “a speed that”. Repetition: “The new policy is a policy that sets new rules” becomes “The new policy sets limits on phones.” Parallelism: a mixed list becomes three matching infinitives.
caption: Give every pronoun a clear antecedent, cut empty repetition, match list forms.

alt: The Gettysburg passage with devices labelled: “we can not” repeated three times, the escalating synonyms dedicate, consecrate and hallow, “it” referring to “this ground”, “consecrated” returning in the second sentence, and the paired opposites “add or detract”.
caption: Repetition and escalation build denial; the returning word makes the turn.
